market_summary: <cite index="29-2,29-3">US markets closed higher on October 5, with the Nasdaq reaching an intraday record high as a weaker-than-expected September jobs report eased concerns about potential interest rate hikes, reducing expectations for another Fed hike in October.

items.headline: US Markets Hit Records as Jobs Data Ease Fed Rate Hike Concerns
items.summary: Nasdaq Composite and Nasdaq-100 set fresh records with tech stocks leading the rally. September payrolls increased by just 29,000, below expectations, supporting speculation the Federal Reserve will hold rates steady in October.

items.headline: SGX Reduces Board Lots for Blue-Chip Stocks to 10 Shares, Lowering Retail Entry Barriers
items.summary: Singapore Exchange cut minimum board lot sizes for 11 blue-chip stocks including DBS, OCBC, and UOB from 100 shares to 10 shares, reducing minimum cash outlay and improving accessibility for retail investors.

items.headline: SGX Shares Fall to Lows as Valuations Concern Major Brokers
items.summary: Singapore Exchange shares declined further, erasing $4.2 billion in market value since August peak. Citigroup cut price target to S$17.70 with sell rating, JPMorgan moved to neutral, and Macquarie went to underperform.

items.headline: Nasdaq 100 Hits Record Highs on AI Stock Strength
items.summary: Tech stocks led market rally with Nvidia, Meta, Microsoft and Tesla all advancing despite higher Treasury yields. Nasdaq-100 reached all-time high as investors shrug off bond market concerns.
